body:
Findings of the two-way review of v3.2.0..HEAD (UI/flows and data/sync). No P1.

## P2

1. **The due date is not gated per account.** A phone with an account on a 3.4.0 server keeps a
   date it set locally forever (the old server drops the unknown field; the pulled row without
   `due` keeps the local date and clears dirty) and never says so — against the AGENTS.md rule that
   a feature needing a newer server is gated per account, never assumed. Fix: a per-account
   capability `supportsDueDates` = (the server's version is known and ≥ 3.5.0) OR (a pulled item
   carried a `due` field, present with any value). Store `serverVersion` on the account row (from
   `/app-version` at the floor check and on every update check) and a `dueDatesSeen` flag set by
   the sync engine on the first pulled item that carries `due`; schema 12 → 13 (add-column
   migration + test). The item dialog offers the Due field only when the capability holds; an item
   that already has a date on an unsupporting account keeps showing it on the row (it is local
   truth) but the dialog shows it read-only with the hint "Due dates need server 3.5.0" (nine
   locales, Android only — the web ships with its server). Server: the `no_app_package` 404 body
   also carries `"version"` (additive; docs) so a server without an APK can be recognised too.
   Tests: the capability from version, from a pulled item, from neither; the dialog gating.
   `docs/wire-contract.md` "Protocol version": one sentence on how a client detects `due` support.

## P3, same pass

2. `SyncEngine.newestClockDevice` must skip the server's own sentinel `updated_by` values
   (`server-merge`, `server-orphan`, `server-list-delete`, see the wire contract's reserved
   literals) when picking the newest clock, else a name-merge or a list-delete cascade makes this
   phone's own edit look foreign to its other account. Test with a merged survivor.
3. No test pins that `deleted` takes part in the self-edit filter: add one (this device last edited
   the note, another account deletes on the web → notified).
4. `TuppuSyncWorker` runs the invite check after every trigger; skip it while
   `AppForegroundState.isForeground` (the overview fetches invites itself) so the "Last invite
   check" line stops reading "app in foreground" nearly always, and requests are saved. Test.
5. `web/src/lib/brandColors.test.ts`: anchor the Kotlin pattern to whole lines (`^val … = Color(0x…)$`,
   multiline) so a commented-out line cannot match first; parse the CSS tokens only inside the two
   `:root { }` blocks; extend the "no colour outside index.css" check to named colours and
   `oklch(`/`color-mix(`/`hwb(`.
6. Android text drawn in `colorScheme.primary` is unreadable since T-324 (2.9:1): the confirmation
   messages on the Account screen and Settings ("Password changed." etc.) and About's update line.
   Use `onSurfaceVariant` for confirmations (as the web does) and `accentText` for the update line.
   Theme-level: Material `TextButton`s (dialog confirm/dismiss, the due-date button) default their
   label to `primary`; set the theme's text-button content colour to `accentText` in `Theme.kt` so
   every dialog button is readable, with a ThemeTest.
7. The re-sign-in screen never shows the server message: `refreshRegistrationStatus()` runs only
   from init when no account is being re-signed. Fetch it for the account's own URL in RESIGNIN
   mode (registration toggle stays hidden there) and again after a submit that confirmed a new
   address failed. Tests.
8. A failed admin reset leaves the previous user's password on screen (Android): clear
   `resetEmail`/`resetPassword` when a reset starts, as the web does. Test.
9. The registration switch's colours (`#2E7D32`, white) are hard-coded in `AdminScreen.kt`; move
   them beside `BalancePositive*` in `Theme.kt` as meaning colours and pin them in the colour test
   (the web has them as tokens already; the parity test may include them).
title: Review follow-ups since 3.2.0: due dates gated per account by server capability, self-edit filter vs server sentinels, readable accent text, re-sign-in server message, small gaps
